questions.query: I consent to participate in this treatment group survey about investment attitudes and preferences
questions.text:
Research Study Consent - Treatment Group Survey

Study Title: Resource Allocation and Child Development Study - Treatment Group

Purpose: You have been randomly assigned to the treatment group. This survey examines your attitudes and preferences regarding investment decisions for children with different abilities.

What you will do: Answer questions about your investment philosophy, decision-making factors, and hypothetical scenarios involving resource allocation between children. This should take approximately 10-15 minutes.

Treatment Group Procedures: As part of the treatment group, you will be presented with specific scenarios and decision-making frameworks that may influence your responses.

Risks and Benefits: There are minimal risks. You may find some questions thought-provoking regarding parenting decisions. The research will contribute to understanding of family investment behaviors.

Confidentiality: Your responses will be kept strictly confidential and used only for research purposes. Group assignment and responses will be anonymized.

Voluntary Participation: Participation is voluntary. You may withdraw at any time without affecting your participation in other parts of the study.

Contact: If you have questions about this research or your rights as a participant, please contact the research team.
This survey examines your attitudes about investing in {child1name} (ability: {child1ability}, attends {child1school}) and {child2name} (ability: {child2ability}, attends {child2school}).

questions.query: In your own words, describe your philosophy about investing in {child1name} and {child2name}'s education and development.
When making investment decisions between {child1name} and {child2name}, how do you typically approach their different abilities?
values: Invest more in the higher-ability child
Invest more in the lower-ability child
Invest based on each child's specific needs
I don't have a consistent approach
